metadata.name: Cytokine Signaling Network
metadata.description: Comprehensive cytokine-receptor interaction and downstream signaling network for autoimmune disease research. Covers major pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory cytokine families, their receptors, adaptor proteins, kinases, and transcription factors. Edges represent binding, activation, inhibition, and downstream signaling relationships with disease associations and literature references.

records.description: TNF-alpha binds TNFRSF1A (TNFR1) to activate NF-kB, MAPK, and apoptotic signaling cascades
TNF-alpha binds TNFRSF1B (TNFR2) to promote cell survival and immune regulation via TRAF2 recruitment
TNFR1 recruits TRADD as the primary adaptor protein via death domain interactions
TRADD recruits TRAF2 to form complex I, leading to NF-kB activation and cell survival signaling
TRADD recruits FADD to form complex II, initiating the extrinsic apoptosis pathway
FADD recruits and activates pro-caspase-8 via death effector domain interactions, initiating the caspase cascade
Activated caspase-8 cleaves and activates executioner caspase-3, committing the cell to apoptosis
TRAF2 activates the IKK complex leading to IkB degradation and NF-kB nuclear translocation
TNFR2 directly recruits TRAF2 without TRADD, activating NF-kB and JNK pathways
IL-1beta binds IL-1R1 initiating pro-inflammatory signaling through MyD88-dependent pathway
IL-1beta binding to IL-1R1 recruits IL-1RAcP co-receptor to form the active signaling complex
The IL-1R1/IL-1RAcP complex recruits MyD88 adaptor protein via TIR domain interactions
MyD88 recruits IRAK4 via death domain interactions, initiating kinase signaling
IRAK4 phosphorylates and activates IRAK1, propagating the IL-1 signaling cascade toward TRAF6
Activated IRAK1 associates with TRAF6, leading to TAK1 activation and downstream NF-kB/MAPK signaling
IL-6 binds membrane-bound IL-6R (classic signaling) or soluble IL-6R (trans-signaling) to initiate gp130-mediated signaling
IL-6/IL-6R complex induces homodimerization of gp130 (IL6ST), the signal-transducing receptor subunit
gp130 dimerization activates constitutively associated JAK1, initiating JAK-STAT signaling
gp130 also activates JAK2, which cooperates with JAK1 in IL-6 signal transduction
JAK1 phosphorylates STAT3 at Y705, enabling dimerization, nuclear translocation, and transcriptional activation of acute-phase genes
IL-12p35 (IL12A) and IL-12p40 (IL12B) form the heterodimeric IL-12p70 cytokine that drives Th1 differentiation
IL-12p40 subunit binds IL-12Rbeta1, the shared receptor chain between IL-12 and IL-23
IL-12p35 subunit interacts with IL-12Rbeta2, the IL-12-specific receptor chain
IL-12Rbeta1 activates TYK2, which cooperates with JAK2 to phosphorylate STAT4
TYK2 phosphorylates STAT4, driving Th1 gene expression including IFNG production
IL-23p19 (IL23A) pairs with IL-12p40 (IL12B) to form the heterodimeric IL-23 cytokine that maintains Th17 cells
IL-23p19 subunit binds IL-23R, the IL-23-specific receptor chain expressed on Th17 cells
IL-23R activates JAK2, which phosphorylates STAT3 to drive Th17 lineage gene expression
JAK2-mediated STAT3 phosphorylation downstream of IL-23R sustains IL-17A and IL-22 production in Th17 cells
IL-17A binds IL-17RA, the shared receptor subunit for IL-17 family cytokines, to drive neutrophilic inflammation
IL-17F binds IL-17RA with lower affinity than IL-17A, contributing to mucosal immunity and inflammation
IL-17RA heterodimerizes with IL-17RC to form the functional receptor complex for IL-17A and IL-17F
IL-17RA recruits ACT1 (TRAF3IP2) via SEFIR domain interactions, the essential adaptor for IL-17 signaling
ACT1 functions as an E3 ubiquitin ligase and recruits TRAF6, leading to NF-kB and C/EBP activation
TRAF6 activates the TAK1-IKK axis to drive NF-kB-dependent transcription of pro-inflammatory genes including CXCL8 and CCL20
IFN-alpha binds IFNAR1 subunit of the type I IFN receptor to initiate antiviral and immunomodulatory signaling
IFN-alpha engages IFNAR2 as the high-affinity receptor chain, forming the heterodimeric IFNAR complex
IFN-beta binds IFNAR1 with distinct kinetics compared to IFN-alpha, influencing differential gene induction
IFN-beta engages IFNAR2 with higher affinity than IFN-alpha subtypes
IFNAR1 activates TYK2, the Janus kinase constitutively associated with the IFNAR1 subunit
IFNAR2 activates JAK1, the Janus kinase constitutively associated with the IFNAR2 subunit
JAK1 phosphorylates STAT1 at Y701 downstream of type I IFN receptor activation
JAK1 phosphorylates STAT2 at Y690, which is specific to type I and type III IFN signaling
Phosphorylated STAT1 and STAT2 heterodimerize via SH2 domain interactions
STAT1-STAT2 heterodimer associates with IRF9 to form the ISGF3 complex that binds ISREs and drives interferon-stimulated gene expression
IFN-gamma homodimer binds two IFNGR1 chains, the ligand-binding component of the IFN-gamma receptor
Ligand-bound IFNGR1 recruits two IFNGR2 chains to complete the active receptor complex
IFNGR1 activates JAK1, which is constitutively associated with the intracellular domain of IFNGR1
IFNGR2 activates JAK2, which is constitutively associated with IFNGR2 and cooperates with JAK1
JAK2 phosphorylates STAT1 at Y701 downstream of IFN-gamma signaling, forming STAT1 homodimers (GAF) that bind GAS elements
IL-2 binds IL-2Ralpha (CD25) with low affinity; CD25 expression defines regulatory T cells and high-affinity IL-2 responsiveness
IL-2 binds IL-2Rbeta (CD122), the beta chain shared with IL-15 receptor that is essential for signal transduction
IL-2Rbeta heterodimerizes with common gamma chain (IL-2Rgamma/CD132), the shared chain for IL-2, IL-4, IL-7, IL-9, IL-15, and IL-21
IL-2Rbeta activates JAK1 upon receptor engagement, initiating the JAK-STAT signaling cascade
Common gamma chain activates JAK3, which is exclusively associated with this receptor subunit
JAK3 phosphorylates STAT5A, driving expression of FOXP3, BCL2, and cell cycle genes critical for T cell survival
JAK3 phosphorylates STAT5B, which cooperates with STAT5A to regulate T cell proliferation and Treg homeostasis
IL-15 signals through IL-2Rbeta and common gamma chain, sharing downstream signaling with IL-2 but with distinct biological outcomes
IL-15 binds IL-15Ralpha with high affinity for trans-presentation to cells expressing IL-2Rbeta/gamma-c
IL-4 binds IL-4Ralpha, the shared receptor chain for type I (IL-4Ralpha/gamma-c) and type II (IL-4Ralpha/IL-13Ralpha1) receptor complexes
IL-4Ralpha activates associated JAK1, which phosphorylates STAT6 to drive Th2 differentiation
Type I IL-4R complex recruits JAK3 via the gamma-c chain to cooperate with JAK1 in STAT6 phosphorylation
JAK1 phosphorylates STAT6 at Y641, driving expression of GATA3, IgE class switching, and Th2 cytokine genes
IL-13 binds the type II receptor complex containing IL-4Ralpha, sharing STAT6 signaling with IL-4
IL-13 first binds IL-13Ralpha1, then recruits IL-4Ralpha to form the type II IL-4R/IL-13R signaling complex
IL-13Ralpha1 associates with and activates TYK2, contributing to downstream STAT6 signaling
IL-10 binds IL-10Ralpha with high affinity, initiating anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive signaling
IL-10-bound IL-10Ralpha recruits IL-10Rbeta (IL-10R2) to form the active tetrameric receptor complex
IL-10Ralpha activates associated JAK1 kinase upon receptor complex formation
IL-10Rbeta activates TYK2, which cooperates with JAK1 to phosphorylate STAT3
TYK2 cooperates with JAK1 to phosphorylate STAT3, which drives anti-inflammatory gene expression including IL10 and SOCS3
IL-10 signaling suppresses NF-kB-dependent pro-inflammatory gene transcription, contributing to immune homeostasis
BAFF (TNFSF13B) binds BAFF-R (TNFRSF13C) with highest specificity, the primary receptor for B cell survival signaling
BAFF binds TACI (TNFRSF13B), a receptor shared with APRIL that regulates T-independent antibody responses and class switching
BAFF binds BCMA (TNFRSF17) with lower affinity than BAFF-R; BCMA is critical for long-lived plasma cell survival
APRIL (TNFSF13) binds TACI (TNFRSF13B) to promote plasma cell survival and IgA class switch recombination
APRIL binds BCMA (TNFRSF17) with higher affinity than BAFF, serving as the primary ligand for plasma cell maintenance
BAFF-R engagement leads to TRAF3 degradation, releasing NIK to activate the non-canonical NF-kB pathway essential for B cell survival
IL-8 (CXCL8) binds CXCR1 with high affinity, driving neutrophil chemotaxis and activation at sites of inflammation
IL-8 binds CXCR2 which also responds to other ELR+ CXC chemokines, mediating neutrophil recruitment and angiogenesis
MCP-1 (CCL2) binds CCR2 to recruit monocytes and macrophages to sites of tissue inflammation
IP-10 (CXCL10) binds CXCR3 to recruit Th1 cells and effector T cells to inflamed tissues; induced by IFN-gamma
RANTES (CCL5) binds CCR5 to recruit T cells, monocytes, and eosinophils; CCR5 is also an HIV-1 co-receptor
CCR2 couples to Gi-alpha (GNAI2) to inhibit adenylyl cyclase and activate PI3K/Akt and MAPK pathways for cell migration
CXCR3 signals through Gi-alpha proteins to drive chemotaxis of effector T cells toward CXCL10-producing tissues
STAT3 directly binds the IL17A promoter and is essential for Th17 cell differentiation and IL-17A production
STAT4 directly transactivates the IFNG locus, driving IFN-gamma production in Th1 cells and NK cells
STAT6 drives GATA3 expression and Th2 cytokine gene locus accessibility, creating a positive feedback loop for IL-4 production
STAT5A binds the FOXP3 promoter and CNS2 enhancer, essential for Treg cell development and homeostasis
STAT1 homodimers (GAF) bind the GAS element in the IRF1 promoter, amplifying interferon-stimulated gene expression
NF-kB directly transactivates the TNF gene promoter, creating a positive feedback loop in chronic inflammation
NF-kB binds the IL6 promoter to drive IL-6 transcription; IL-6 is a major NF-kB target gene in inflammation
NF-kB drives transcription of pro-IL-1beta, which requires inflammasome-mediated cleavage for secretion of active IL-1beta
NF-kB is a major transcriptional activator of CXCL8 (IL-8), linking pro-inflammatory signaling to neutrophil recruitment
IFN-gamma potently induces CXCL10 transcription via STAT1/IRF1, creating a feedforward loop that recruits more Th1 cells
IL-6/STAT3 signaling induces SOCS3 expression, which provides negative feedback by binding gp130 to suppress further signaling
SOCS3 binds JAK1 kinase domain and gp130 receptor to inhibit IL-6/JAK1/STAT3 signaling as a negative feedback mechanism
SOCS1 directly binds the activation loop of JAK2 to inhibit IFN-gamma and other cytokine signaling pathways
IL-17A and IL-17F form homodimers and heterodimers (IL-17A/F), with the heterodimer having intermediate biological activity
TRAF2 activates TAK1 (MAP3K7) through K63-linked polyubiquitin chains, a key node linking TNF to NF-kB and MAPK pathways
TAK1 activates JNK1 (MAPK8) via the MKK4/MKK7 cascade, leading to AP-1-mediated gene expression
TAK1 phosphorylates and activates the IKK complex (IKKbeta), leading to IkBalpha degradation and NF-kB nuclear translocation
IL-12Rbeta2 activates JAK2 upon IL-12 binding, which cooperates with TYK2 from IL-12Rbeta1 to phosphorylate STAT4
JAK2 cooperates with TYK2 to phosphorylate STAT4 downstream of IL-12, driving Th1 differentiation and IFN-gamma production
IL-1alpha binds IL-1R1 to initiate the same signaling cascade as IL-1beta; IL-1alpha also functions as an alarmin from necrotic cells
IL-1Ra (IL1RN) competitively binds IL-1R1 without recruiting IL-1RAcP, acting as a natural antagonist of IL-1 signaling
STAT3 directly transactivates BCL2 and BCL2L1 (BCL-XL), promoting cell survival and resistance to apoptosis
STAT3 binds the MYC promoter to drive proliferation, linking IL-6 signaling to cell cycle progression in lymphocytes
STAT1 homodimers drive CXCL9 (MIG) transcription via GAS elements, recruiting CXCR3+ T cells to inflamed tissues
CCR5 signals through Gi-alpha proteins to activate chemotaxis, integrin activation, and cytoskeletal rearrangement
CXCR1 couples to Gi-alpha protein to mediate neutrophil chemotaxis, degranulation, and respiratory burst
FOXP3+ Tregs are dependent on IL-2 for survival; FOXP3 modulates IL-2 signaling components and enhances IL-2 sensitivity via CD25 upregulation
FOXP3 promotes IL-10 production in regulatory T cells, a key mechanism of Treg-mediated immune suppression
IL-21 signals through a receptor complex containing IL-21R and common gamma chain, sharing JAK1/JAK3/STAT3 signaling
IL-21 activates STAT3 as its primary signaling mediator, promoting B cell differentiation and Tfh cell function
TGF-beta1 binds TGF-beta receptor type II (TGFBR2), which recruits and transphosphorylates TGFBR1 (ALK5)
TGFBR2 phosphorylates and activates TGFBR1 (ALK5) in the GS domain, enabling SMAD2/3 recruitment and phosphorylation
Activated TGFBR1 phosphorylates SMAD3 at the C-terminal SXS motif, enabling nuclear translocation and target gene regulation
TGF-beta induces FOXP3 expression in naive T cells via SMAD3 binding to the FOXP3 enhancer, driving induced Treg differentiation
TGF-beta in combination with IL-6 induces RORgamma-t (RORC) expression, the master transcription factor for Th17 differentiation
RORgamma-t directly transactivates the IL17A and IL17F gene loci, serving as the lineage-defining factor for Th17 cells
STAT3 activation is downstream of IL-6 classic and trans-signaling via the JAK1/JAK2-gp130 axis
STAT4 phosphorylation is downstream of IL-12 signaling through TYK2 and JAK2 kinases
NF-kB activation is downstream of IL-1beta/IL-1R1 signaling via the MyD88-IRAK4-IRAK1-TRAF6 cascade
STAT1 homodimer (GAF) formation is downstream of IFN-gamma/IFNGR signaling through JAK1 and JAK2
STAT6 Y641 phosphorylation is downstream of IL-4/IL-4Ralpha signaling via JAK1 and JAK3
STAT3 phosphorylation is downstream of IL-10/IL-10R signaling via JAK1 and TYK2, mediating anti-inflammatory gene induction
STAT5A phosphorylation is downstream of IL-2/IL-2R signaling via JAK1 and JAK3, critical for Treg survival
STAT3 activation is downstream of IL-23/IL-23R signaling via JAK2, sustaining Th17 cell maintenance and pathogenicity
ISGF3 complex (STAT1/STAT2/IRF9) assembly is downstream of IFN-alpha receptor signaling via JAK1 and TYK2
